title: Add atomic chrooted offline bundles with apt/dnf snapshot pinning and rollback detector
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: Customers in highly-regulated on-prem environments asked for smaller, auditable offline bundles that can be applied atomically in chrooted install environments while preserving package provenance and enabling safe rollback. Existing vendor bundles include full OS layers which are heavy and hard to verify; this change introduces a new 'chrooted bundle' format and an installer-side rollback detector that compares package manifests and signature trees.

What this PR does: introduces a compact, layered offline bundle format that: (1) contains signed apt/dpkg and dnf/rpm manifests with exact-version pins; (2) supports 'ephemeral chroot' application mode where packages are installed into a temporary root and switched over atomically; (3) integrates with our registry mirror/apt-proxy Terraform inputs; (4) adds a preflight 'rollback-detector' job that validates the resulting filesystem against the signed manifest and aborts if divergence is detected; (5) exposes CLI flags to validate signatures and run chroot dry-runs.

Implementation notes: implemented bundle composer in tools/bundle/compose_chroot.go that produces a layered tar.xz (metadata.json, signed-manifests/, apt-index.tar.xz, dnf-modules.tar.xz, layer-00.tar.xz ...). The installer (cmd/installer/chroot_apply.go) applies layers into an ephemeral chroot using pivot-root patterns, writes a transaction marker, runs package-manager verification hooks, and then atomically flips the symlink for /opt/redwood/runtime -> /opt/redwood/runtime.active. Terraform module redwood-terraform/modules/registry-mirror now includes variables 'apt_proxy_host' and 'dnf_module_pin' and a new output 'mirror_index_checksum' used to verify mirror integrity. Helm chart change: charts/private-installer/templates/deamonset-airgap.yaml sets imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent and adds nodeSelector airgap:true for better scheduling in isolated clusters.

Checklist: - [x] Compose and sign apt/dnf manifests with GPG keys managed by installer KMS integration. - [x] Ephemeral chroot apply with transaction marker and atomic switch. - [x] Terraform inputs for apt/dnf mirror and index checksum. - [x] Helm chart imagePullPolicy and tolerations for air-gapped nodes. - [x] Unit tests for manifest verification and rollback-detector. - [x] Integration test using local k3s in-airgap simulating mirror mismatch.

Backwards compatibility: bundles produced with the previous format remain supported; installer detects legacy bundles and falls back to the non-chroot path. Increased bundle verification is opt-in via the --chroot-mode and --strict-verify flags so operators can stage the change.

Operational guidance (summary): To build an atomic chroot bundle locally: tools/bundle/compose_chroot --out /tmp/bundle-atomic.tar.xz --gpg-key <key-id> --apt-repo /var/lib/apt-mirror --dnf-modules /var/lib/dnf-mirror. To apply on an air-gapped node: redwood-install --bundle /tmp/bundle-atomic.tar.xz --chroot-mode --strict-verify --apt-proxy 127.0.0.1:3142. Rollback detection logs live under /var/log/redwood/rollback-detector.log and will surface a non-zero exit code to the installer if mismatch is detected.

Related work: builds on ENG-1531 (delta bundles), INF-287 (signed bundle verification), and the Terraform mirror work in ENG-1799.

release_notes: Add support for atomic chrooted offline bundles: signed apt/dnf manifests, ephemeral chroot apply, Terraform mirror inputs, Helm airgap scheduling tweaks, and rollback detection. Backwards compatible; opt-in via --chroot-mode and --strict-verify.
